My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know this soil. I know what grows here and what the market wants. My husband works in town now — the factory pays better — so I manage the fields mostly myself, with help from neighbors during busy times.

We have 6 mu of flat dryland. I will do what I always do and what everyone here does: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same plots. This rotation is reliable. I know the rhythm of it. Wheat goes in the ground in October after the autumn rains, maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. Two harvests from the same land — that's how you make the land work for you.

For wheat I will use the seed from last year's harvest that I kept — the variety from the village seed station, everyone uses it, it does well in our soil. For maize I will buy hybrid seed from the township supply shop, same brand as last three years, Zhengdan 958. It yields well and the grain dries properly.

I apply fertilizer the same way my mother-in-law taught me — base fertilizer before planting, then a top-dress in spring for wheat, and I throw urea on the maize after it's knee-high. I irrigate wheat three times: before freeze-up, when it joints, and when it heads. Maize I irrigate once or twice depending on the summer rain. This summer has been dry lately so probably twice.

I don't have money to hire machines for everything so I will use the village rotary tiller service for wheat planting prep. For maize I will seed directly — no need to till again, the soil is fine after wheat.

I also keep a small vegetable patch near the house, half a mu, for our own eating. Mainly garlic, Chinese cabbage, beans. I do not track this carefully — it is just for the family.
